kid.question: What does the Lord say Cyrus will help rebuild?

options.text: Babylon’s idols
Jerusalem and its temple
A wall around Egypt
A new sea road

kid.explanation: The Lord names Cyrus as an instrument for rebuilding Jerusalem and releasing captives, though Cyrus has not known Him.

kid.question: For whose sake does the Lord say He called Cyrus?

options.text: The image makers
Only Cyrus’s family
Jacob and Israel
Babylon’s astrologers

kid.explanation: The Lord calls Cyrus for Israel’s sake so people across the earth may know that He alone is God.

kid.question: What does the Lord invite to spring up together?

options.text: Gold and silver
Horses and chariots
Prisons and chains
Righteousness and salvation

kid.explanation: The Lord claims authority over light, darkness, peace, and calamity, then calls for righteousness and salvation.

kid.question: What does Isaiah compare a person arguing with the Maker to?

options.text: Clay arguing with its potter
A sheep following its shepherd
A child learning from a teacher
A traveler finding a road

kid.explanation: The clay-and-maker image warns against treating the Creator as if the created thing controlled Him.

kid.question: What happens to the captives in the Lord’s plan?

options.text: They are sold for gold
They are set free
They build new prisons
They remain in Babylon

kid.explanation: The one raised up will rebuild the city and release captives without demanding a price.

kid.question: Who is promised lasting salvation?

options.text: The carved images
The image makers as makers
Israel in the Lord
The gates of brass

kid.explanation: Idol makers are shamed, while Israel is promised enduring salvation in the Lord.

kid.question: Why did God form the earth in this passage?

options.text: To remain empty
To house only idols
To hide His voice
To be inhabited

kid.explanation: The Creator formed the earth to be inhabited and says He did not tell Jacob to seek Him in vain.

kid.question: Who is invited to look to the Lord and be saved?

options.text: All the ends of the earth
Only the idol makers
Only Jerusalem’s rulers
Only people already free

kid.explanation: The Lord contrasts images that cannot save with His invitation to all the ends of the earth to look to Him and be saved.

kid.question: Where does Isaiah say strength is found?

options.text: In a goldsmith
In the Lord
In a gate of brass
In an idol’s wood

kid.explanation: The Lord declares universal acknowledgment of Him and says righteousness and strength are in Him.

kid.question: Who carries whom in the Lord’s promise?

options.text: The idols carry their makers
The animals carry the Lord
The Lord carries His people
Cyrus carries every idol

kid.explanation: The idols must be carried by animals, while the Lord promises to carry and deliver His people through old age.

high-school.question: What is surprising about Cyrus being called by name?

options.text: Cyrus is one of Isaiah’s sons
Cyrus asks to become a prophet
The Lord uses him even though he has not known the Lord
Cyrus has already rebuilt every city

high-school.explanation: The Lord names Cyrus as an instrument for rebuilding Jerusalem and releasing captives, though Cyrus has not known Him.

high-school.question: What wider purpose accompanies the Lord’s action for Israel?

options.text: Cyrus may be worshipped in every nation
Israel may hide its identity
Each region may choose a separate creator
People from east to west may know He alone is God

high-school.explanation: The Lord calls Cyrus for Israel’s sake so people across the earth may know that He alone is God.

high-school.question: What does the range from light to darkness stress?

options.text: The Lord governs both ease and hardship
The Lord is unable to bring peace
Darkness belongs to a rival god
The people must worship the sky

high-school.explanation: The Lord claims authority over light, darkness, peace, and calamity, then calls for righteousness and salvation.

high-school.question: What is the point of the clay’s question to its maker?

options.text: A potter cannot choose a design
A creature lacks the maker’s perspective and authority
Clay has better plans than a potter
All questions are forbidden

high-school.explanation: The clay-and-maker image warns against treating the Creator as if the created thing controlled Him.

high-school.question: Why does “not for price nor reward” matter to the release promise?

options.text: The captives must pay after returning
The city cannot be rebuilt with money
Deliverance is not presented as a transaction for payment
Only wealthy people will be freed

high-school.explanation: The one raised up will rebuild the city and release captives without demanding a price.

high-school.question: What contrast organizes these verses?

options.text: Shame for Israel and triumph for idols
Equal salvation through every image
Equal failure for the Lord and the idols
Shame for idol makers and lasting salvation for Israel

high-school.explanation: Idol makers are shamed, while Israel is promised enduring salvation in the Lord.

high-school.question: How do creation’s purpose and the call to seek God reinforce each other?

options.text: God’s work and words have a meaningful end
God made an empty earth but changed His mind
Seeking God is meant to fail
Creation is unrelated to the people’s hope

high-school.explanation: The Creator formed the earth to be inhabited and says He did not tell Jacob to seek Him in vain.

high-school.question: What makes the invitation wider than Israel’s earlier promise?

options.text: It is given only to Cyrus
It is addressed to all the earth
It excludes those who made idols
It is limited to Jerusalem’s walls

high-school.explanation: The Lord contrasts images that cannot save with His invitation to all the ends of the earth to look to Him and be saved.

high-school.question: What does every knee bowing signify in the passage?

options.text: The end of all human movement
Cyrus becoming the only king
Recognition of the Lord’s rightful authority
The idols gaining equal honor

high-school.explanation: The Lord declares universal acknowledgment of Him and says righteousness and strength are in Him.

high-school.question: What is the key contrast between the idols and the Lord?

options.text: Both must be carried by animals
The idols answer while the Lord is silent
The Lord remains fixed while idols travel
People carry idols; the Lord carries people

high-school.explanation: The idols must be carried by animals, while the Lord promises to carry and deliver His people through old age.

expert.question: How does “though thou hast not known me” qualify the title given to Cyrus?

options.text: Cyrus’s mission depended on recognizing every prophecy
The title makes Cyrus a second covenant God
The Lord’s plan was discovered by Cyrus first
Divine appointment does not imply Cyrus personally understood the Lord

expert.explanation: The Lord names Cyrus as an instrument for rebuilding Jerusalem and releasing captives, though Cyrus has not known Him.

expert.question: How do the particular and universal aims fit together in verses 4–6?

options.text: Calling Cyrus for Israel also discloses the Lord’s uniqueness worldwide
Helping Israel prevents other peoples from knowing God
The worldwide claim makes Israel irrelevant
Cyrus is selected only to teach geography

expert.explanation: The Lord calls Cyrus for Israel’s sake so people across the earth may know that He alone is God.

expert.question: How should the paired claims about opposite conditions be read beside the call for salvation?

options.text: The opposites establish two equal divine powers
The Lord governs the whole historical scene while directing it toward righteousness
The passage says calamity itself is the final good
The call for salvation narrows God’s authority to weather

expert.explanation: The Lord claims authority over light, darkness, peace, and calamity, then calls for righteousness and salvation.

expert.question: How does the potter image support the following creation claim?

options.text: The earth is literally a clay vessel
The people’s objections prove the Maker has no purpose
The Maker’s authority precedes the creature’s judgment of His work
Cyrus becomes the potter who created the heavens

expert.explanation: The clay-and-maker image warns against treating the Creator as if the created thing controlled Him.

expert.question: How does the unpriced release connect Cyrus’s role to the Lord’s purpose?

options.text: The Lord sells the captives to a kinder ruler
The city is rebuilt only after tribute is collected
Cyrus is promised the temple as a personal prize
The ruler’s action serves divine restoration rather than private profit

expert.explanation: The one raised up will rebuild the city and release captives without demanding a price.

expert.question: How does “everlasting salvation” answer the temporary prestige of idols?

options.text: The Lord’s rescue outlasts the false objects and their makers
An image becomes everlasting once made of gold
The promise depends on hiding God forever
The makers’ shame is itself Israel’s salvation

expert.explanation: Idol makers are shamed, while Israel is promised enduring salvation in the Lord.

expert.question: What argument against futility links “not in vain” to “Seek ye me”?

options.text: The world’s purpose can be found only by Cyrus
The purposeful Creator has not issued an empty invitation
The Lord’s speech is deliberately secret
The invitation is limited to those who already know the answer

expert.explanation: The Creator formed the earth to be inhabited and says He did not tell Jacob to seek Him in vain.

expert.question: How does the image that “cannot save” sharpen the open invitation in verse 22?

options.text: The image must first teach the nations to look
The invitation asks nations to carry their idols to Jerusalem
A powerless alternative is set against salvation offered by the one God to all
Salvation depends on which wooden image is chosen

expert.explanation: The Lord contrasts images that cannot save with His invitation to all the ends of the earth to look to Him and be saved.

expert.question: How does universal acknowledgment relate to Israel’s being justified in the Lord?

options.text: Only Israel bows while the nations remain outside
Acknowledgment transfers the Lord’s power to idols
Israel becomes righteous by its own military success
Both rest on the Lord as the source of righteousness and strength

expert.explanation: The Lord declares universal acknowledgment of Him and says righteousness and strength are in Him.

expert.question: Why is the repeated “carry” language central to the argument?

options.text: Idols burden carriers; the Lord bears His people
Both sides rely equally on human shoulders
The animals become the true redeemers
The passage concerns the cost of moving statues

expert.explanation: The idols must be carried by animals, while the Lord promises to carry and deliver His people through old age.
